card.keepWhy: No map. Just the next step.
sources: Genesis 12:1-3 (the call: leave your country, your relatives and your father’s house; “I will make of you a great nation… you will be a blessing”)
Genesis 12:4 (Abram went; he was seventy-five years old when he left Haran)
Genesis 12:5 (he took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother’s son, and all their possessions)
Genesis 12:6-7 (arrival in Canaan; “I will give this land to your offspring”; Abram builds an altar); the altar is behind the today step
Genesis 17:5 (renamed Abraham, “father of a multitude of nations”)
Hebrews 11:8 (he went out, not knowing where he was going), behind the teach line
check: Hard-one answer reads the later honor of Abraham by Jews, Christians and Muslims as the promise coming true “far beyond one family”; confirm this framing is acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever felt too old, or too late, to start over?
options: then this one is for you. listen closely.
then you’ll know this feeling. listen.
good. keep this one for someone you love who does.

steps.line: Abram lived in a city called Haran. He had a home, his family and his flocks. Life was settled.
Then God said to him, “Leave your country, your relatives and your father’s house, and go to the land I will show you.”
steps.label: Genesis 12:1

steps.q: God says go, but doesn’t say where. What does God give him instead?
o: A map of the road ahead
A sign to follow, like a star
steps.why: No map and no sign. Just a promise (Genesis 12:2). And Abram doesn’t ask a single question back. Genesis only says: “So Abram went.”

steps.line: No map. No address. Just a promise: “I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you, and you will be a blessing.”
steps.label: Genesis 12:2

steps.q: God promises Abram a great nation. What makes that promise hard to believe?
o: He is too poor to feed a tribe
He and Sarai have no children
steps.why: Genesis says it plainly just before the call: “Sarai was barren; she had no child” (11:30). A great nation, promised to a childless couple.

steps.line: So Abram went. He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot and everything they had, and set out.

steps.q: As he leaves, the Bible stops to tell us one thing about Abram. Your guess?
o: How far he planned to go
steps.why: His age: seventy-five (Genesis 12:4). Genesis rarely stops for a detail like that on the road, so readers have long paid attention when it does.

steps.line: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
steps.label: Genesis 12:4

steps.q: Why might the story bother to tell us he was seventy-five?
o: To explain why he took Lot along to help
To mark when the family records began
To show it wasn’t too late for him to begin
steps.why: Many readers hear it that way. He wasn’t young and he wasn’t sure of the road. He started anyway.

steps.line: At last they reached the land of Canaan. God said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” And Abram built an altar there.
steps.label: Genesis 12:7

steps.q: Haran was in what is now southern Turkey. How far was Canaan, on foot with flocks?
steps.why: Roughly 400 miles (650 km) as the crow flies, and farther on the road. At a flock’s pace, that’s well over a month of walking with no address at the end.

say: here’s what i love. abram didn’t get a map. he got a promise, and he took the first step anyway.
christians read him as a picture of faith: he went out not knowing where he was going. faith here means the next step, not the whole road.

steps.q: God didn’t only say “I will bless you.” He said “you will be a blessing.” What’s the difference?
o: He’d be rewarded only after death
The gift was meant to pass through him
He would have to earn it by sacrifice
steps.why: The next line says it: “in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed” (Genesis 12:3). Today Jews, Christians and Muslims all look back to Abraham.

today.say: abram marked his new start with an altar. today, before one new thing you begin, stop for a moment and hand it to God, in your own words or in silence, if you’d like. or simply notice the step.
options: that’s how abram’s road started. one step, offered up.
that counts. you’ve named the step. the road starts there.
